dealAnnounced: Practice jersey patch and official healthcare partnership announced August 2023 (replacing Rothman Orthopaedics on patch); Jefferson Health Training Complex naming rights announced February 17, 2026 (replacing NovaCare Complex name in use since 2001); multiyear extension of partnership

financials.source: Thomas Jefferson University consolidated audited financial statements FY2025 and Becker's Hospital Review (Aug 2025). Total revenue rose 57.6% YoY due to Lehigh Valley Health Network merger (closed Aug 1, 2024; 11 months included). Operating loss of $196M (-1.2% margin); $170M of that loss attributable to Jefferson Health Plans (GLP-1 drug costs). Excluding insurance arm, operating loss was $25.6M. Total assets in thousands per audit: $18,291,623. Non-operating investment income of ~$271M per Fitch. FY2024 operating income was ~$1.3M (essentially breakeven). FY ends June 30. ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer: EIN 23-1352651.

balanceSheetWealth.investmentPortfolioSource: Russell Investments case study (c. 2023): Jefferson investment office oversees 'over $4 billion of non-qualified and qualified assets' plus $2.2 billion in defined contribution assets. FY2024 audit shows investments held by Methodist Hospital Foundation and Magee Rehabilitation Hospital Foundation totaling ~$3.92B (a subset of system total). Endowment payout was $150.1M in FY2024 (up from $134.9M in FY2023); net realized/unrealized gains of $247.6M in FY2024.
balanceSheetWealth.realEstateSource: Not verified — check Philadelphia, Montgomery, Bucks, Delaware county (PA) and Camden, Burlington, Gloucester county (NJ) property assessment records for tax-exempt holdings across 18+ hospital campuses
balanceSheetWealth.notes: Thomas Jefferson University is the parent entity and holds the endowment and investment portfolio for the combined Jefferson enterprise. The university merged with Philadelphia University in 2017. Jefferson Health now operates 18+ hospitals across Pennsylvania and New Jersey following mergers with Abington Health (2015), Aria Health (2016), Kennedy Health (2018), Einstein Healthcare Network (2021), and Lehigh Valley Health Network (2024). Post-LVHN merger, total assets jumped from ~$11.8B to ~$18.3B.

bondDebt.issuerAuthority: Philadelphia Authority for Industrial Development (PAID); Pennsylvania Economic Development Financing Authority (PEDFA)
bondDebt.source: Thomas Jefferson University consolidated audited financial statements FY2025: total revenue bonds $5,077,672 (in thousands), up from $3,440,830 in FY2024. Total long-term debt obligations $5,282,201 (in thousands). Increase reflects assumption of LVHN debt in merger. Historical PEDFA issues include Series 1998A ($141.6M) and Series 2005B ($54.4M), likely since refunded. EMMA (emma.msrb.org) has series-level detail by obligor.

communityBenefit.source: Jefferson Health website: 'nearly $754 million in charitable care and community benefit (FY24).' Percentage estimated against ~$10B consolidated operating revenue for FY2024. Includes charity care, medical education, subsidized health services, research, prevention/screening programs, and in-kind grants — charity care alone not broken out in available sources. FY2020 total was $448M per earlier Jefferson report. Pennsylvania requires Act 55 community benefit reporting. Check Form 990 Schedule H for individual hospital entities for charity care line items.

taxAdvantage.notes: Jefferson Health operates 18 hospitals across multiple Pennsylvania and New Jersey counties. Tax-exempt property holdings span Philadelphia, Montgomery, Bucks, and Delaware counties in PA plus Camden, Burlington, and Gloucester counties in NJ. Pennsylvania's Institutions of Purely Public Charity Act (Act 55 of 1997) governs nonprofit hospital property tax exemptions. Bond debt is issued through public authorities (PAID, PEDFA) generating tax-exempt interest subsidies. Multiple Jefferson hospitals qualify as DSH for 340B program participation.

layoffs.source: Fierce Healthcare; Philadelphia Inquirer; Healthcare Finance News; Newsweek

keyRiskFactors: All three agencies moved to Negative outlook in late 2025 / early 2026
Fitch cited $170M loss from Jefferson Health Plans (Medicaid managed care) and expects 'measured recovery' over 24-36 months
Moody's cited margins below expectations and likelihood of further liquidity decline; days cash on hand fell from ~140 to ~114
S&P cited magnitude of operating losses and 'anticipated difficulties in returning to or near operating profitability for several years'
Rapid merger-driven expansion — six major mergers (2015-2024 including LVHN) creating ongoing integration risk across $16B enterprise
$5.1B in tax-exempt revenue bonds outstanding (FY2025), up from $3.4B pre-LVHN merger
High-profile NFL sponsorship spending (Eagles jersey patch, training complex naming) amid $196M operating loss and ~1,000 layoffs in 2025

ratios.investmentsToOperatingIncomeInterpretati: Not meaningful — Jefferson posted a -$196M operating loss in FY2025. Investment portfolio (~$4B) represents ~20x the absolute value of the operating loss, indicating substantial accumulated wealth despite sustained operating deficits.
ratios.bondDebtToCommunityBenefitInterpretation: For every $1 of claimed community benefit ($754M FY2024), Jefferson carries $6.73 in tax-exempt bond debt ($5.08B FY2025). Bond debt increased 48% in one year due to LVHN merger.
ratios.charityCareVsStateInterpretation: Cannot isolate charity care from the $754M community benefit total; figure includes medical education, research, and subsidized services. Pennsylvania state average charity care percentage not available from search.

accusation: Jefferson Health — a $15.8 billion system built through six mergers in nine years, now carrying $5.1 billion in tax-exempt bond debt — paid its CEO $6.9 million and secured Eagles jersey patch sponsorship and training complex naming rights while posting a $196 million operating loss in FY2025, cutting approximately 1,500 jobs across four rounds of layoffs (2023-2025), and drawing Negative outlooks from all three credit rating agencies. The system sits on an investment portfolio exceeding $4 billion and claimed $754 million in community benefit, yet the bulk of its operating deficit came from its own Medicaid managed care plan (Jefferson Health Plans, -$170M), not from charity care. All of this under the shelter of its 501(c)(3) status as Thomas Jefferson University (EIN 23-1352651), which exempts it from federal, state, and local taxes and allows it to issue tax-exempt bonds.
